editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece with a clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. 782 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Every bullet in 'What We Know' is individually attributed to a specific outlet, and the article is careful to distinguish figures that come from different tests (e.g. the 84%/13% figure vs. the separate 90%/23% comparison) rather than conflating them.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read in full from local gzip snapshots (sha256 of decompressed content verified against manifest.json for all 4 files — all matched exactly, all fetched with HTTP 200, no archive fallback needed). (1) sources/2026-07/.../source-0.html.gz (MIT Technology Review, 'Meet GPT-Red...') confirms: GPT-Red as internal LLM attacker built via self-play, the fake-chain-of-thought discovery, the Choquette-Choo '1+1=3' quote verbatim, the Hunn quotes verbatim, the Kandpal 'risk surface/blast radius' quote verbatim, the Vendy/Andon Labs test, the GPT-5 vs GPT-5.6 90%/23% figures with GPT-5 dated 'August last year' (=August 2025, correctly resolved by the article since this MIT TR piece published July 15, 2026), and that OpenAI will not release GPT-Red. (2) source-1.html.gz (SiliconANGLE) confirms: 84%/13% success-rate figure verbatim, the 'sixth of the rate...four months earlier' / 6x figure, the fake-chain-of-thought 95%->10% figure verbatim, the Hunn and Kandpal quotes (attributed to MIT Technology Review by SiliconANGLE itself, correctly reflected in the article), and the Vendy agent compromise. (3) source-2.html.gz (Decrypt) confirms: the self-play training description and the exact 'GPT-Red learns through adversarial self-play...' OpenAI quote, the 84%/13% figure, the Vendy case study (lowering prices, ordering discounted inventory, canceling an order) with vulnerabilities disclosed and addressed, and the 'GPT-Red will remain an internal tool because it contains intentionally developed offensive capabilities' line verbatim. (4) source-3.html.gz (Help Net Security) confirms: the GPT-5.1 84% indirect-injection figure, the Vendy real-world test with the exact $0.50 price-floor detail verbatim, the 6x-fewer-failures / 'GPT-5.6 Sol' framing verbatim, the fake-chain-of-thought 'below a tenth' quote verbatim, the 97% indirect-injection accuracy and 0.05% direct-injection failure figures verbatim, and the closing OpenAI quote about scaling compute for future GPT-Red versions verbatim. No hallucinated quotes, no misattributed specifics, and no orphan body URLs outside article.sources found across any of the four snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, name, and direct quote in the body traces exactly to one of the four cited outlets. The article correctly flags in 'What We Don't Know' that the 84%/13% figure (SiliconANGLE/Decrypt) and the separate 90%/23% figure (MIT Technology Review) come from methodologically distinct tests rather than presenting them as a single consistent statistic — this is an accurate and appropriately cautious editorial call given the sources genuinely describe different test setups. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attribution-heavy throughout; no editorializing or sensationalism. Appropriately hedges with an explicit 'What We Don't Know' section noting OpenAI's own blog/X post was not independently accessible and that figures are drawn from secondary reporting.
